tabs.tab1_description:
13 Mukhi Nepalese Rudraksha is a bead of unlimited joy in all material and non-material aspects of life. It holds immense power to eliminate illusions that prevent and bind a person from achieving his desires. The wearer attains and meets only what he or she truly desires, thereby eliminating many meaningless things and relationships from the path and attracting only what truly moves the wearer's heart. The 13 mukhi rudraksha is ruled by the planet Venus or Shukra in Sanskrit, which means "clear" or "bright", thus, this rudraksha removes blurry intentions, aligning the wearer with what he or she truly desires to accomplish. The wearer of the 13 mukhi Nepal rudraksha is blessed with dynamism, magnetism, success, worldly desires and spiritual growth. It enables a person to take the right decisions and actions in life. He or she is endowed with the attributes of the Kamadeva or Cupid God, granting them divine charisma and immense power. As a result, wearing 13 mukhi rudraksha is extremely effective for achieving all kinds of material goals in life, removing inappropriate long-term desires, and clarifying a person's true aspirations for their own good. For example, when we desire to be married in order to feel supported, to find the right job in order to realize our full potential, to desire money for sustenance or food in order to nourish, all of these right intentions are attained sooner or later by the wearer of 13 mukhi rudraksha. In general, this bead facilitates and soothes all unions when there is good intent behind them. Only as a result of Lord Kamadeva’s intervention did Lord Shiva marry Goddess Parvati and become a householder.

As per Shiv Puran by wearing a 13 mukhi rudraksha, one achieves the satisfaction of all (innermost) desires, as well as good luck and fortune. According to the Padma Puran, the wearer of this bead is also blessed with wealth and success.

Scriptural Reference of 13 mukhi Rudraksha

Shiva Purana. Chapter 25, Sloka 79.

Trayodashamukho vishvedevastaddharanannarah | 
Sarvankamanavapnoti saubhagyam mangalam labhet || 79 ||
Thirteen faced Rudraksha is the form of Vishvedeva. Person who attires this Rudraksha will have all wishes fulfilled and gain good fortune and luck. 

(Padma Puranam, Srishti-Khanda 59, verses 191b–194)

यद्येकं लभते मर्त्यस्त्रयोदशमुखं रुद्राक्षं रुद्रदैवतम्।
सर्वकामप्रदं श्रेष्ठं मङ्गलं परमं स्मृतम्॥

कर्तिकेय! सुभाग्यवान् रसायनं च सिद्ध्यति।
देवपादुकासिद्धिं च लभते नात्र संशयः॥

मातृपितृस्वसृभ्रातृगुरुघातकृतोऽपि वा।
त्रयोदशमुखं धृत्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते॥
Translation: If a man gets a rudraksha having thirteen mouths, i.e. Rudra, he should know that it is most auspicious and fulfils all desires. O Kartikeya, he endowed with good luck accomplishes the nectar-like elixir, alchemy and the impression of the feet of a deity or a holy person. A man is free from all sins by wearing a rudraksha with thirteen mouths, even if he has killed his mother, father, sister, brother or preceptor (Guru).

13 mukhi Nepal Rudraksha is available in a variety of sizes, including: small, regular, large and collector. The bigger the size of the rudraksha the faster the results. This is because the seeds are bigger and the surface area in contact with skin is larger, thus, energy is dispersed more quickly throughout the body.

How to identify original 13 mukhi Nepal Rudraksha? 

Some fraudulent tests have gained popularity and must be avoided because their results are unreliable and they cannot be used to determine the authenticity of Rudraksha.

The Fake tests are the Water Test, Milk test or Copper Coin Rotation Test. All these tests are unscientific and produce untrustworthy results.

One way to determine the originality of Rudraksha beads is to take an X-ray. In an X-ray, the compartment and seeds inside the Rudraksha are observable, and their number should ideally correspond to the number of Mukhi lines on the bead. Sometimes all seeds are not visible as they get compressed during formation and compartments are very close to each other, though.

Experts at Rudra Centre can examine the bead and determine if they are original or not. You can send us images and videos of your Rudraksha at the email: contact@rudracentre.com for our experts to determine authenticity.

In recent years many labs have emerged which offer Rudraksha certification however these are highly unreliable because they do not have the right knowledge and many times make mistakes in identifying Rudraksha beads. Many traders are using these labs to issue fake certificates. These labs are not able to distinguish manipulated beads where extra lines are carved on the Rudraksha to make it a higher mukhi which costs more. Also, they do not reject beads with incomplete mukhi lines which actually don’t give results. These labs are not affiliated with any central body or government, so they do not have any credibility. Hence to protect consumers Rudra Centre has opened its own laboratory and have started issuing genuine certificate where all parameters 
of the Rudraksha are analyzed. We examine whether the beads are healthy, whether the mukhi lines are complete, and whether the rudraksha beads has been manipulated.

At Rudra Centre, we issue certificates for all beads procured from us. If you want an X-ray certificate for the Rudraksha bead, then an additional INR 500 is charged per Rudraksha bead.

How to Clean & Maintain 13 mukhi Nepal Rudraksha?

Rudraksha beads can last a lifetime and be passed down through generations if cared for properly.

In cold and dry climates, rudraksha beads may develop surface-level cracks, in which case any natural unscented oil may be applied, such as olive oil, sandal oil, or cow ghee.

Rudraksha may develop molds and insects if they are kept in a humid place and unused for a long time, in this case follow the below steps:

  • Dip the Rudraksha beads in lukewarm water for 15 mins.
  • Clean any molds visible of the surface using a toothbrush.
  • Dry them under the shade of the Sun (indirect Sunlight) or you can also use a dryer or hairdryer.
  • After following the above steps, you can start wearing your rudraksha beads or combination again.

Follow the steps below to regularly clean your Rudraksha beads:

  • Wash Rudraksha beads under running water.
  • Scrub the surface of the rudraksha to remove any dust particles caught in the grooves, using a toothbrush.
  • Use the shade of the Sun (indirect sunlight) or a hairdryer to dry the beads.
  • Apply any natural and unscented oil like Olive oil, Almond oil or Sandal oil.
  • If you are planning to not wear beads for a long duration, it is advisable to keep them in the fridge.
  • Do not use any chemical cleaner or insecticide or pesticide to clean or treat your Rudraksha.
  • Do not put your rudraksha beads in boiling water or extremely hot water.

13 mukhi Nepal Rudraksha Health & Color

13 mukhi Nepal Rudraksha will become darker overtime with usage because it is exposed to oil, sweat and the environment, this is a natural process and doesn’t affect the energy of the Rudraksha bead. It is best to choose a light Sandy Brown to Brown color Rudraksha bead as it generally means the bead is healthy and freshly (recently) harvested. It is advised to avoid wearing dark black or dark grey color beads as they may be lifeless. To check if the bead is healthy and alive just shake the bead well and if you hear the seeds inside rattling then it means that the bead is lifeless or dead and if there is no rattling sound then the bead is healthy and alive. You can inspect the bead from all sides and look inside the natural hole to ensure that there are no white color molds or insects which have infested the bead. Sometimes the soap gets stuck in the grooves, which are white in color; therefore, you should determine whether the white deposits are soap or mold. The mold will appear as threads whereas the soap deposits will be like a cream or paste. The energy of the Rudraksha beads resides is in its seeds, thus we must ensure that the seeds are healthy and alive.
